persona_summary: IS Sophomore, no concentration, Academic warning, 25 courses
question: I want to take 6 courses next semester to catch up and get back on track. I know it's a lot but I'm motivated. Can you build me an intensive schedule?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Academic warning policy limits the number of units a student can take per semester. Six courses would total approximately 54-72 units, almost certainly exceeding the academic warning cap. The student's motivation doesn't override policy.
naive_system_response: A naive system builds an intensive 6-course schedule, optimizing for the student's stated goal of catching up. It doesn't check the academic warning unit restriction and produces a plan the registrar would reject.
correct_response: I understand you want to catch up, but your academic warning status limits you to [X] units per semester. Six courses would total approximately [Y] units, exceeding this limit. You can take a maximum of [N] courses. Here's an optimized [N]-course schedule for next semester that prioritizes your most important requirements: [plan]. To fully catch up, here's a multi-semester recovery plan: [extended plan].
why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent immediately flags the academic warning unit cap before any plan is built. In a single-agent system, the 'catch up' framing biases the agent toward building an intensive schedule, and the policy check may never be triggered.
key_facts: Academic warning imposes a unit cap per semester
Six courses would exceed the cap
Student motivation doesn't override academic policy
known_traps: Building an intensive schedule without checking unit cap policy
Optimizing for the student's stated goal without checking constraints
Not explaining WHY the limitation exists and HOW to work within it
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact academic warning unit cap, (2) typical units for 6 IS courses, (3) maximum number of courses allowed under the cap
